newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ukraine plans Eurobond in three to four months.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans Eurobond in three to four months.

text.p: Ukraine plans to launch a Eurobond in three or four months, shortly after its foreign bond debut on the Japanese market in September, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of reforms Serhiy Tyhypko said on Tuesday.

"We expect to launch the Eurobond in three to four months," Tyhypko told Reuters during an investor conference in Frankfurt. "Deutsche Morgan Grenfell will be the lead manager for Ukraine's Eurobond and we will also work with JP Morgan, which will be the rating consultant," he added.
Tyhypko gave no issue volume or denomination for the Eurobond, which he confirmed was due to follow Ukraine's planned September bond debut on the Japanese market.

The minister said he did not expect statements last week by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which said it may issue an interim stand-by credit until Ukraine fulfilled conditions for a long-term multi-billion dollar credit, to affect the former Soviet republic's potential rating.
"That won't influence our rating. I think there will be a large demand for our bonds," Tyhypko said.
He added Ukraine was trying to convince the IMF to issue the $2.5 to $3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility.

Central bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko said previously Ukraine wanted to raise $300 to $900 million by tapping foreign bond markets, in part to cover the budget deficit set at four percent of gross domestic product by Western calculations.
